beats.headline: Employees only, says the dwarf
beats.text: For the record: car five of the yellow line train is the conductor's, and the conductor is Vernon, dwarf, level 32, drinking. His duties are to take care of the train and to be in charge of its employees. In practice the engineer does not listen to him, the janitors try to eat him and the porters are in their own little world, so he drinks until the end of the line and then does it again. He asks the crawlers to leave. Then he notices Princess Donut is royalty, salutes, and his drink goes flying.

beats.headline: The loop, as far as he knows it
beats.text: At station 435 everything goes fuzzy, and subject finds himself on the platform at station 10, the yard, climbing aboard again. He cannot say how much time has passed. He is not looping himself, he reasons, because a Brain Amoeba scar stayed with him; the train is, because a bottle poured out returns to its shelf. A Goateo once stayed aboard past 435 and was found as a skeleton. The engine car is locked. Nobody gets in without an engineer's key.

beats.headline: Ten gold, every trip
beats.text: Anything aboard on his first day resets each loop, and anything he carries stays with him. So subject has a jacket full of identical drawings of his wife, and several hundred gold grown from the ten coins on his nightstand: each trip pays him the equivalent of ten trips. He could go home from the yard any time. He is staying until he cannot hold any more gold, before one of the other dwarfs finds out and tries to weasel onto his train, and then he means to go home to his wife. One day.

beats.headline: Fire ants in car five
beats.text: Station 116. Crawler Carl unzips Princess Donut's prize suitcase on subject's counter, and the Find Traps notice arrives too late. Literal Fire Ants, level 1, pour out in impossible numbers, and the drawings of his wife are the first thing to burn. The moonshine explodes. The crawlers get out through car four onto the platform. Subject does not. A flaming wave sweeps over him, and the train picks up speed and disappears into the tunnel, burning.

beats.headline: No wife, says Carl
beats.text: Crawler Katia says what there is to say: poor Vernon, he was saving up money to buy his wife a new house. Princess Donut's complaint is that the bugs burned up her prize. Crawler Carl answers both. There is no wife, he says, and there was no prize; the ants were the prize. He resolves to train his Find Traps skill, which did warn him, but much too late.

beats.headline: A memory with nothing under it
beats.text: Crawler Carl reopens the file while questioning Madison, an employee who has been putting in a lot of mandatory overtime. When Vernon told him about his wife, Carl had taken her for a made-up phantom. Now he has a theory to put under it: this floor's NPCs were given false memories without a proper foundation, stories as paper-thin as the background of an NPC in an actual game. Asked whether she has ever been to her own apartment, Madison says of course she has. It has just been a few days.
